brief.subject: Freight demand up nearly 5%, rejections near 13%, diesel $6.292
brief.headline: Freight Demand Jumps Nearly 5% as Spot Rates Keep Climbing; Diesel Dips to $6.292
brief.dek: Tighter truckload capacity, a small diesel dip, a lame-duck Congress clock and an $11.4 million theft lead today's brief.
brief.lede: Freight demand rose nearly 5% week over week, tender rejections are near 13%, and spot rates are still climbing.

sections.heading: Demand up, capacity tightening
bullets: Nearly 5%: weekly freight demand gain, giving carriers more loads to choose from.
Near 13%: tender rejection rate, meaning more contract freight is spilling into the spot market.
Van contract and spot rates are both rising, a good moment to push for stronger linehaul offers.
Flatbed and LTL conditions were also tracked, with spot markets strengthening in some areas.

sections.heading: Diesel slips, still up for month
bullets: $6.292 per gallon: U.S. average retail diesel for the week of 2026-11-02.
Down 6.0 cents (0.9%) from the prior week, a small break at the pump.
Up 9.3 cents over four weeks, so fuel surcharges still matter in rate talks.

sections.heading: Congress clock runs out Jan. 3
bullets: Noon, Jan. 3, 2027: any trucking bill not passed by both chambers and sent to the president dies.
Election results shifted the political math, with Democrats winning control, changing odds for pending trucking legislation.
Unfinished bills would restart next Congress with new numbers and new committee chairs.

sections.heading: $11.4M load vanishes in transit
bullets: $11.4 million: reported value of NVIDIA hardware that disappeared between California and Texas.
Oakland police are investigating it as grand theft; the carrier's identity remains unclear.
High-value electronics remain a top theft target, so vetting and load security deserve extra attention.

sections.heading: West Coast ports: strike delayed
bullets: LA-Long Beach terminal watchmen and employers pushed back a strike deadline as contract talks continue.
A walkout could still disrupt drayage and container flow out of the nation's busiest port complex.
343%: rise in Asia-U.S. West Coast container spot rates since the Iran war began, per Xeneta.
